assessment: This valuable study by Cui et al. investigates mechanisms generating sighs, which are crucial for respiratory function and linked to emotional states. Utilizing advanced methods in mice, they provide solid evidence that increased excitability in specific preBötzinger complex neuronal subpopulations expressing Neuromedin B receptors, gastrin-releasing peptide receptors, or somatostatin can induce sigh-like large amplitude inspirations. With additional technical clarifications and further elaboration of the limitations in terms of how the results are interpreted in the revised manuscript, the study will interest neuroscientists studying respiratory neurobiology and rhythmic motor systems.
